newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin predicts summit will be his hardest ever.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin predicts summit will be his hardest ever.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin said on Friday next week's Russia-U.S. summit would be the hardest since he became Russian president in 1991 but that he was ready for compromise, Interfax news agency said.
The talks "will be the hardest in all the history of Russian-American relations", Yeltsin was quoted as telling Russian media chiefs.

"I do not rule out that we may disagree on something. The Russian leadership's position is well known -- we do not intend to make compromises which would weaken the country's defence capability," Yeltsin said of the summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton in Helsinki on March 19-20.
But he said compromise was possible at the summit, which is expected to be dominated by discussion of the row over NATO's plans to expand eastwards which Russia says would threaten its security.

"In a recent telephone conversation Clinton made clear the United States is interested in compromise, and so am I. We are for a compromise which would not abuse the security of the Russian Federation," Yeltsin said.
